hypothesis: Layer 3 (Little's law with tau = F/P): stars that pass once through the upper red giant branch and the horizontal branch have a common formation rate, so R = N_HB/N_RGB(above ZAHB) = tau_HB/tau_RGB from stellar models. Second test of the T002 claim with independent star counts and a stellar-model error fixed in advance.

observable.quantity: R = N_HB / N_RGB(above ZAHB), constant value for the 8 in-situ Galactic globular clusters
observable.domain: Gontcharov et al. 2026 sample (HST ACS + Gaia DR3, entire cluster fields)

prediction_method.description: R_pred = 6.26 Y - 0.12 with Y = Y_HII_Aver (from the Ayala record, as in T002); sigma_tot^2 = (6.26 sigma_Y)^2 + sigma_model^2 + sigma_obs^2 with sigma_model = 0.029 from Cassisi et al. 2003 ranges (t002_model_systematics.py) and sigma_obs the observed error on the side facing R_pred; z = |R_pred - R_obs| / sigma_tot.

fixed_parameters: sigma_model = 0.0294 (12C(alpha,gamma) and breathing-pulse ranges of Cassisi et al. 2003, uniform, in quadrature)
common formation rate b for RGB and HB
fail_criterion: z > 3 -> FAILED; 2 < z <= 3 -> INCONCLUSIVE (reported as tension, not pass)
note: Disclosure: drafted after reading the source abstract and conclusions, which state R = 1.31 for in-situ clusters and interpret it as anomalous HB energy loss; the outcome is therefore effectively computable before approval and this is not blind. The comparison script has not been run. Independence: different telescopes (HST ACS and Gaia, not WFPC2), membership cleaning and ZAHB cut from the Salaris et al. 2004 counts behind T002. Caveats that the author should weigh before approving: (1) the source warns that R_th(Y) of Ayala et al. may be incomplete and that R differs between cluster centres and peripheries (HB depleted after disk crossings, recovering in 60-80 Myr); in layer-3 terms that is a breakdown of the steady state that Little's law needs, so the test also probes the steady-state assumption; (2) only 8 clusters; (3) sigma_model comes from 2003 models and may be smaller with newer 12C(alpha,gamma) rates (Ayala et al. argue a white-dwarf compensation limits it). Not UET-distinct: standard stellar evolution passes or fails in the same way. Re-check transcribed numbers against the journal version before approval.
